A task force is a unit or formation established to work on a single defined task or activity.
WFSBP Task Forces provide some of the most important**scientific aspects of the WFSBP**.
Each Task Force is represented in the list below and includes its members and scientific inputs.
Should you be interested in becoming involved in the WFSBP and particularly a certain Task Force, please contact us directly by emailing info@wfsbp.org.
*   To review documents from other jurisdictions that have addressed this issue and to learn from and build upon their recommendations and experience.

*   To review the current literature on best practices in managing mental disorders in primary care and collaboration between primary care and mental health care providers and determine its applicability for this project.
*   To identify specific resources which could be of value to practitioners in any country or community.
*   To circulate draft documents broadly for review before the document is presented to the WFBSP.

*   To enhance recognition of the concept of Neuroprogression, its clinical significance and the different diagnostic and treatment stages among professionals through continuing medical education and presentations at conferences.

*   To produce a consensus paper on the definition of the concept of Neuroprogression and its clinical relevance to personalized diagnosis, treatment and prevention of chronicity of psychiatric disorders.
*   To publish papers addressing clinical perspectives of Neuroprogression addressing clinical perspectives, biological mechanisms, psychosocial factors and preventive interventions.
*   To provide, periodically, progress reports to the WFSBP executive on the activities of the group.
*   Elucidating the etiology and pathogenesis of insomnia and other sleep disorders, particularly in relation to psychopathology.
*   Determining sleep-wakefulness patterns and their aberrations in various psychiatric disorders and neurologic diseases.
*   Optimizing the management (diagnosis, treatment and prevention) of sleep – wakefulness disorders.
*   Treatment guidelines in the context of the comprehensive management of insomnia and other sleep-wakefulness disorders.
*   To facilitate the establishment of an international research network on suicidal behaviour (WORECA).
*   To provide, periodically, progress reports to the WFSBP executive on the activities of the group.
